statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of Alcohol, Drugs, or a Combination of Both
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first/second); Class A Misdemeanor (with injury or child passenger); Third Degree Felony (third+ or with serious injury)
penalty_max: 6 months (Class B); 364 days (Class A); 5 years (Third Degree Felony)
elements: Defendant operated or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
Within the state
While under the influence of alcohol, any drug, or combination of alcohol and any drug
To a degree that renders the person incapable of safely operating a vehicle
Or had a BAC of .05 or higher
mandatory_minimum: 48 consecutive hours or 48 hours community service (first); drug/alcohol screening
enhancements: Bodily injury to another (Class A Misdemeanor)
Passenger under 18 and defendant 21+ (Class A Misdemeanor)
Third or subsequent conviction within 10 years (Third Degree Felony)
Prior automobile homicide conviction (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Utah has the nation's lowest BAC limit at .05. Implied consent under Utah Code § 41-6a-520. License suspension: 120 days (first), 2 years (second+). Drug and alcohol screening required.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
penalty_min: 48 consecutive hours imprisonment or 48 hours community service
elements: Defendant operated or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or combination
BAC .05 or higher, or impairment of ability to safely operate
No prior DUI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 48 consecutive hours imprisonment or 48 hours community service; drug/alcohol screening
notes: 120-day license suspension. Ignition interlock may be ordered. Must complete screening and recommended treatment.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (second); Third Degree Felony (third+ within 10 years)
penalty_min: 240 hours community service or 5 days imprisonment plus 30 days electronic monitoring (second)
elements: Defendant operated or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or combination
BAC .05 or higher, or impairment of ability
One or more prior DUI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 5 days imprisonment plus 30 days electronic monitoring or 240 hours community service (second)
enhancements: Third offense within 10 years (Third Degree Felony)
Prior automobile homicide conviction (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Second offense: 2-year license revocation. Third+ within 10 years is a Third Degree Felony. Ignition interlock required.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_min: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of any drug or combination of alcohol and any drug
To a degree rendering the person incapable of safely operating a vehicle
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Any measurable controlled substance or metabolite in the body (per se violation under § 41-6a-517)
notes: Utah has a metabolite DUI law — any measurable amount of a controlled substance metabolite in the body while driving is a per se violation, even without impairment.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common DUI plea-down. Adds points to driving record.

statute_title: Duty to Stop and Render Aid — Accident Involving Injury or Death
offense_class: Third Degree Felony (injury); Second Degree Felony (serious injury or death)
elements: Defendant was the operator of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, serious injury, or death
Defendant failed to immediately stop at the scene
Defendant failed to render reasonable assistance and provide identification
enhancements: Serious bodily injury or death (Second Degree Felony)
notes: Hit-and-run involving property damage only (§ 41-6a-401.3) is a Class B Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony (DUI-related); Third Degree Felony (criminally negligent)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
In a criminally negligent manner or while under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or with BAC .05+
Proximately caused the death of another person
notes: Automobile homicide while DUI is a Second Degree Felony. Automobile homicide by criminal negligence without intoxication is a Third Degree Felony.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle in a criminally negligent manner
Causing the death of another person
notes: Utah does not have a separate vehicular manslaughter statute. Vehicular deaths are charged as automobile homicide.

statute_title: Driving While License Denied, Suspended, Disqualified, or Revoked
offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (first); Class B Misdemeanor (second within 3 years); Class A Misdemeanor (third+ within 3 years)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a highway
While the defendant's license was denied, suspended, disqualified, or revoked
Defendant had notice of the denial, suspension, disqualification, or revocation
notes: Additional period of suspension added upon conviction.

statute_title: Failure to Respond to Officer's Signal to Stop — Fleeing
offense_class: Third Degree Felony
elements: Defendant was operating a motor vehicle
A peace officer signaled the defendant to stop
Defendant willfully failed to stop or attempted to flee by vehicle or other means
enhancements: Creating substantial risk of serious injury
notes: Fleeing from police in a vehicle is a Third Degree Felony. License revocation of 1 year.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (marijuana under 1 oz, first/second); Class A Misdemeanor (Schedule III-V); Third Degree Felony (Schedule I/II)
penalty_max: 6 months (Class B); 364 days (Class A); 5 years (Third Degree Felony)
elements: Defendant knowingly and intentionally possessed a controlled substance
Unless obtained by a valid prescription
The substance was listed in the schedules
enhancements: Possession near school, park, or church (enhanced)
notes: Utah reformed drug possession laws. Simple possession of small amounts may qualify for drug court or diversion programs.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (under 1 oz, first/second); Class A Misdemeanor (under 1 oz, third+); Third Degree Felony (1 oz to 1 lb)
penalty_max: 6 months (Class B); 364 days (Class A); 5 years (Third Degree Felony)
elements: Defendant knowingly and intentionally possessed marijuana
Amount determines classification
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense for under 1 oz (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Utah has a medical cannabis program but recreational marijuana remains illegal. Possession of under 1 oz is a Class B Misdemeanor for first and second offenses.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly and intentionally possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Without lawful authorization
notes: Possession of any amount of cocaine is a Third Degree Felony.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly and intentionally possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Without lawful authorization
notes: Meth is a major enforcement concern in Utah. Possession of any amount is a Third Degree Felony.

statute_title: Production, Manufacturing, or Distribution of Controlled Substance
offense_class: Second Degree Felony (Schedule I/II); Third Degree Felony (Schedule III/IV)
elements: Defendant knowingly and intentionally produced, manufactured, distributed, or possessed with intent to distribute
A controlled substance
The substance was listed in the schedules
enhancements: Distribution within 1,000 feet of a school, park, church, or library
notes: Enhanced penalties for drug-free zone violations. Distribution to a minor carries enhanced penalties.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony (Schedule I/II); Third Degree Felony (Schedule III/IV)
elements: Defendant distributed or dispensed a controlled substance
To another person
notes: Distribution and manufacturing fall under the same statute section.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony (Schedule I/II); Third Degree Felony (Schedule III/IV)
elements: Defendant knowingly and intentionally manufactured a controlled substance
Including producing, preparing, compounding, or processing
enhancements: Manufacturing meth (Clandestine Drug Lab Act penalties)
notes: Utah Clandestine Drug Lab Act provides additional penalties for meth labs including environmental cleanup liability.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant used or possessed with intent to use drug paraphernalia
To introduce a controlled substance into the body
notes: Delivery of paraphernalia is a Class A Misdemeanor. Delivery to a minor is a Third Degree Felony.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony (Schedule I/II); Third Degree Felony (Schedule III/IV)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With intent to distribute
Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, or other circumstances
notes: Intent to distribute inferred from large quantities, packaging materials, scales, large amounts of cash, and communications.

offense_class: First Degree Felony (capital offense)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused the death of another

Under one or more aggravating circumstances (murder of peace officer, during commission of aggravated robbery/burglary/kidnapping/sexual assault, murder for hire, multiple victims, prior murder conviction, etc.)
notes: Utah abolished the death penalty in 2023. Aggravated murder carries mandatory 25 years to life without parole or life without parole.

offense_class: First Degree Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused the death of another
Or acting under circumstances evidencing depraved indifference to human life, engaged in conduct creating a grave risk of death that caused the death
Or committed or attempted to commit a felony and in the course thereof a death occurred
notes: Murder is a First Degree Felony carrying 5 years to life. Includes depraved indifference murder and felony murder.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another
Or caused the death of another under the influence of extreme emotional disturbance (reasonable explanation or excuse)
notes: Manslaughter includes reckless killings and killings under extreme emotional disturbance (heat of passion).

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant caused the death of another
With criminal negligence
notes: Negligent homicide is the lowest level of criminal homicide in Utah. Covers unintentional deaths from criminal negligence.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony; Second Degree Felony (serious bodily injury or loss of consciousness)
elements: Defendant committed assault as defined in § 76-5-102
And used a dangerous weapon or other means or force likely to produce death or serious bodily injury
Or caused serious bodily injury
notes: Aggravated assault causing serious bodily injury is a Second Degree Felony.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (substantial bodily injury)
elements: Defendant attempted, with unlawful force or violence, to cause bodily injury to another
Or committed an act with unlawful force or violence that caused or created a substantial risk of bodily injury
Or committed a threat of violence against another accompanied by a show of immediate force or violence
notes: Simple assault is generally a Class B Misdemeanor. Elevated to Class A if substantial bodily injury results.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant committed an act with unlawful force or violence
That caused bodily injury to another
notes: Utah combines assault and battery under the single assault statute. No separate battery offense.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant unlawfully and intentionally took or attempted to take personal property
In the possession of another
From the person or immediate presence against the person's will
By means of force or fear
notes: Robbery is a Second Degree Felony. Aggravated robbery (§ 76-6-302) is a First Degree Felony.

offense_class: First Degree Felony
elements: Defendant committed robbery as defined in § 76-6-301
And used or threatened to use a dangerous weapon
Or caused serious bodily injury to another
notes: Aggravated robbery is a First Degree Felony with 5 years to life. One of the most seriously punished property/violent crimes.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly, without authority of law and against the will of the victim
Detained or restrained the victim for any substantial period of time
notes: Aggravated kidnapping (§ 76-5-302) involving ransom, use as shield, serious bodily injury, or sexual assault is a First Degree Felony.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony (habitation or occupied structure); Third Degree Felony (other property valued $1,500+)
elements: Defendant, by means of fire or explosives, unlawfully damaged
A habitation, building, or other property
Whether the property belonged to the defendant or another
enhancements: Habitation or occupied structure (Second Degree Felony)
notes: Aggravated arson (§ 76-6-103) involving occupied buildings with knowledge of occupancy is a First Degree Felony.

offense_class: First Degree Felony (attempted murder); Second Degree Felony (attempted aggravated murder)
elements: Defendant intended to commit murder
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward commission
The victim survived
notes: Criminal attempt for a First Degree Felony is a Second Degree Felony. However, attempted murder and aggravated murder have specific enhanced penalties.

statute_title: Aggravated Assault with a Dangerous Weapon
offense_class: Third Degree Felony
elements: Defendant committed assault
Using a dangerous weapon or other means of force likely to produce death or serious bodily injury
enhancements: Serious bodily injury resulting (Second Degree Felony)
notes: Dangerous weapon includes firearms, knives, and any instrument capable of causing death or serious bodily harm.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (under $500); Class A Misdemeanor ($500-$1,500); Third Degree Felony ($1,500-$5,000); Second Degree Felony ($5,000+)
penalty_max: 6 months to 15 years depending on value
elements: Defendant obtained or exercised unauthorized control over property of another
With a purpose to deprive the owner thereof
notes: Utah consolidates larceny, embezzlement, and false pretenses under a unified theft statute. Value thresholds determine classification.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony ($1,500-$5,000); Second Degree Felony ($5,000+)
elements: Defendant took property of another
The value of the property exceeded $1,500
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Felony theft in Utah begins at $1,500.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (under $500); Class A Misdemeanor ($500-$1,500)
elements: Defendant took property of another
The value of the property was under $1,500
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Petty theft covers thefts under $1,500.

offense_class: Same as theft by value
elements: Defendant took possession of, concealed, or carried away unpurchased merchandise
From a retail establishment
With intent to deprive the merchant of the merchandise without paying
enhancements: Use of device to overcome security system
notes: Penalties follow the same value thresholds as general theft. Civil liability to the merchant also applies.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony
elements: Defendant entered or remained unlawfully in a building or portion of a building
With intent to commit a felony, theft, assault, lewdness, sexual battery, or voyeurism
notes: Standard burglary is a Third Degree Felony. Aggravated burglary (§ 76-6-203) — entering a dwelling with a person present — is a First Degree Felony.

offense_class: First Degree Felony
elements: Defendant committed burglary of a dwelling
While a person other than a participant was present in the building
Or defendant was armed with a dangerous weapon or explosive
Or defendant assaulted someone during the burglary
notes: Aggravated burglary of an occupied dwelling is a First Degree Felony (5 years to life). One of the most serious property crimes in Utah.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony (most vehicles valued $5,000+); Third Degree Felony ($1,500-$5,000)
elements: Defendant obtained or exercised unauthorized control over a motor vehicle
Belonging to another
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Charged under the general theft statute. Most vehicles exceed the $5,000 threshold for Second Degree Felony.

offense_class: Same classification as theft based on value
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of property of another
Knowing that it had been stolen or believing that it probably had been stolen
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Penalties mirror theft classifications based on value of stolen property.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (under $500); Class A Misdemeanor ($500-$1,500); Third Degree Felony ($1,500-$5,000); Second Degree Felony ($5,000+)
penalty_max: 6 months to 15 years depending on damage
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged, defaced, or destroyed property of another
notes: Restitution typically ordered. Criminal mischief is Utah's primary property destruction statute.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (dwelling)
elements: Defendant entered or remained unlawfully on property of another
Knowing or having reason to know the entry was unlawful
enhancements: Trespass of a dwelling (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Trespass of a dwelling is elevated to a Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (under $500); Class A Misdemeanor ($500-$1,500); Third Degree Felony ($1,500+)
penalty_max: 6 months to 5 years depending on damage
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged, defaced, or destroyed property of another
Or recklessly or with criminal negligence caused damage by fire, explosives, or other means
notes: Criminal mischief is Utah's vandalism and property destruction statute.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (simple assault); Class A Misdemeanor (substantial bodily injury); Third Degree Felony (aggravated)
penalty_max: 6 months to 5 years depending on severity
elements: Defendant committed a criminal offense involving violence or physical harm
Against a cohabitant (spouse, former spouse, person residing in same dwelling, person related by blood or marriage, person with shared child)
enhancements: Prior domestic violence convictions within 5 years
notes: Domestic violence is an enhancement to the underlying offense. Mandatory arrest policy. Protective orders available.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (substantial injury)
elements: Defendant committed an act of unlawful force or violence against a cohabitant
Causing bodily injury
notes: Domestic battery is charged under the assault statute with the domestic violence designation. Domestic violence designation triggers mandatory arrest.

statute_title: Endangerment of a Child or Vulnerable Adult
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Third Degree Felony (grave risk)
elements: Defendant, having care or custody of a child
Caused or permitted the child to be exposed to or placed at risk of harm
Or failed to provide necessary care
enhancements: Grave risk of death or serious bodily injury (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Mandatory reporting. DUI with child in vehicle may trigger separate endangerment charges.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (simple); Third Degree Felony (serious physical injury); Second Degree Felony (serious bodily injury)
penalty_max: 364 days (Class A); 5 years (Third Degree); 15 years (Second Degree)
elements: Defendant inflicted physical injury upon a child
Or having care or custody of a child, caused or permitted another to inflict physical injury
Under circumstances likely to produce death or serious injury
notes: Child abuse resulting in death may be charged as homicide.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Third Degree Felony (subsequent within 5 years)
elements: A valid protective order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant intentionally or knowingly violated the terms of the order
enhancements: Second or subsequent violation within 5 years (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Includes domestic violence protective orders, stalking injunctions, and civil protective orders.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Third Degree Felony (subsequent or with prior domestic violence)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly engaged in a course of conduct directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety or suffer emotional distress
enhancements: Second or subsequent conviction (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Includes in-person and electronic/cyber stalking. Stalking injunctions available.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant, with intent to frighten or harass another
Communicated a written or recorded threat to commit a violent felony
Or engaged in a course of conduct that would cause a reasonable person fear
notes: Harassment may escalate to stalking charges with repeated conduct.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of a Vulnerable Adult
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (abuse/neglect); Third Degree Felony (exploitation under $5,000); Second Degree Felony (exploitation $5,000+)
penalty_max: 364 days (Class A); 5 years (Third Degree); 15 years (Second Degree)
elements: Defendant abused, neglected, or exploited a vulnerable adult (65+ or disabled)
The conduct caused harm or risk of harm
Or the defendant financially exploited the victim
notes: Mandatory reporting required. Financial exploitation penalties based on amount.

statute_title: Restrictions on Possession, Purchase, Transfer, and Ownership of Dangerous Weapons
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (minor possession); Third Degree Felony (unlawful transfer)
elements: Defendant possessed or transferred a dangerous weapon
While prohibited by law (minor, convicted felon, mentally ill person, or in prohibited location)
notes: Utah allows permit-less concealed carry for persons 21+ (constitutional carry since 2021). Restrictions apply to prohibited persons and locations.

statute_title: Possession of Dangerous Weapon by Restricted Person
offense_class: Second Degree Felony (Category I — violent felony); Third Degree Felony (Category II — non-violent felony)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly possessed or had under their custody or control a dangerous weapon
Defendant was a restricted person (convicted of a felony, on probation/parole for a felony, etc.)
notes: Category I restricted persons (violent felons) face Second Degree Felony. Category II (non-violent felons, drug offenders) face Third Degree Felony.

statute_title: Carrying a Dangerous Weapon in Prohibited Area
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant carried a dangerous weapon
In a location prohibited by law or a secure area
notes: Prohibited areas include secure areas of airports, courthouses, and mental health facilities.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (general); Class A Misdemeanor (from vehicle or at building); Third Degree Felony (at habitation or vehicle with occupants)
penalty_max: 6 months (Class B); 364 days (Class A); 5 years (Third Degree)
elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
Under circumstances creating a risk of injury or death
enhancements: From or at a vehicle (Class A Misdemeanor)
At an occupied habitation or vehicle (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Discharge at an occupied structure or vehicle is a Third Degree Felony.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony
elements: Defendant obtained personal identifying information of another person
Without authorization
And used or attempted to use that information to obtain credit, goods, services, or other thing of value
notes: Includes Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, bank account numbers, and other personally identifying information.

offense_class: Same as theft by value
elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant obtained or exercised unauthorized control over the property
With purpose to deprive the owner
notes: Embezzlement is consolidated under the general theft statute.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony
elements: Defendant, with purpose to defraud anyone or with knowledge that it is facilitating a fraud
Altered, made, completed, executed, or authenticated any writing so that it purports to be the act of another
notes: Forgery is always a Third Degree Felony in Utah regardless of amount.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony
elements: Defendant made or altered a writing
So that it purports to have value or authenticity it does not have
With purpose to defraud
notes: Counterfeiting is prosecuted under the forgery statute. Federal charges may also apply.

statute_title: Issuing a Bad Check or Draft
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (under $500); Class A Misdemeanor ($500-$1,500); Third Degree Felony ($1,500+)
penalty_max: 6 months to 5 years depending on amount
elements: Defendant issued or passed a check or draft
Knowing it would not be paid by the drawee
With purpose to defraud
notes: Presumption of knowledge if check not made good within 14 days of notice.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly presented false information in connection with an insurance transaction
With intent to defraud an insurer
The information was material
notes: Insurance fraud is a Second Degree Felony in Utah regardless of amount. Includes all types of insurance.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of a Credit Card
offense_class: Same as theft by value obtained
elements: Defendant used a credit or debit card
Knowing it was stolen, forged, expired, or revoked
With intent to defraud
notes: Penalties mirror general theft based on value obtained through fraudulent use.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Involving property the defendant knew was derived from unlawful activity
With intent to promote the unlawful activity or conceal the source
notes: Money laundering is a Second Degree Felony. Also subject to federal prosecution.

offense_class: Same as theft by value
elements: Defendant obtained or exercised control over property by deception
With purpose to deprive the owner
notes: General fraud is prosecuted as theft by deception. Specific fraud statutes also exist for securities, communications, and insurance.

offense_class: First Degree Felony
elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse with the victim
Without the victim's consent
enhancements: Victim under 14 (mandatory 25 years to life under § 76-5-402.1)
notes: Rape in Utah is a First Degree Felony (5 years to life). Rape of a child under 14 carries a mandatory 25 years to life.

offense_class: First Degree Felony
elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse with the victim
Without the victim's consent
Consent is not a defense if victim is under 14
notes: Rape is always a First Degree Felony. Rape of a child (§ 76-5-402.1) carries mandatory 25 years to life.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second+)
elements: Defendant performed an act of lewdness
In a public place or under circumstances which the defendant should know would likely cause affront or alarm
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class A Misdemeanor)
Lewdness involving a child (Third Degree Felony under § 76-9-702.5)
notes: Lewdness involving a child is a Third Degree Felony. May trigger sex offender registration.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (subsequent)
elements: Defendant paid or offered to pay another person for sexual activity
notes: Patronizing a prostitute who is a minor is a Second Degree Felony.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony (possession/distribution); First Degree Felony (production)
elements: Defendant knowingly produced, possessed, or distributed a visual depiction of a minor engaged in sexually explicit conduct
notes: Each image may be charged as a separate offense. Sex offender registration required.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender or Kidnap Offender
offense_class: Third Degree Felony
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender or kidnap offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register, update, or verify registration information
notes: Registration required for 10 years or lifetime depending on offense. Failure to register is always a Third Degree Felony.

statute_title: Unlawful Sexual Activity with a Minor
offense_class: Third Degree Felony (defendant 7+ years older than victim 14-15); Second Degree Felony (defendant 10+ years older)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual activity with a minor
The minor was 14 or 15 years old
The defendant was 4 or more years older
notes: Age of consent in Utah is 18 for persons in positions of authority, 16 generally. Unlawful sexual activity with a minor 14-15 applies when defendant is significantly older.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor; Infraction (if defendant desists on request)
elements: Defendant intended to cause public inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm
Or recklessly created a risk thereof
By engaging in fighting, violent, tumultuous behavior, or making unreasonable noise
notes: Reduced to an infraction if defendant desists upon request by a peace officer.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally interfered with a person recognized to be a law enforcement officer
While the officer was performing any act within the scope of their authority
notes: Does not require physical force — interference by any means is sufficient.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony (capital/first degree felony underlying); Third Degree Felony (other felony); Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor underlying)
penalty_max: 15 years (Second Degree); 5 years (Third Degree); 364 days (Class A)
elements: Defendant, with intent to hinder, delay, or prevent the investigation, apprehension, prosecution, or defense of any person
Provided false information, altered evidence, harbored the suspect, or interfered with proceedings
enhancements: Severity depends on classification of the underlying offense
notes: Obstruction involving a capital or first degree felony investigation is a Second Degree Felony.

offense_class: Punishable by fine and/or imprisonment at the court's discretion
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a court order
Or engaged in disorderly, disrespectful, or insolent behavior in the court's presence
notes: Courts have inherent contempt power. Direct and indirect contempt procedures differ.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant was intoxicated in a public place
To the degree that the defendant was a danger to themselves or others
Or was unreasonably disturbing others
notes: Officers may take to detoxification facility. Utah has a strong temperance culture.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor underlying); Third Degree Felony (felony underlying)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Defendant was required to appear in court
Defendant willfully failed to appear as required
enhancements: Underlying charge is a felony (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Bond forfeiture and bench warrant. Classification depends on the underlying charge.

statute_title: Filing a False or Fraudulent Report with Law Enforcement
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly gave false information to a law enforcement officer
With intent to mislead the officer regarding the commission of a crime
notes: Filing a false report is a Class B Misdemeanor. False emergency reports (§ 76-9-606) carry enhanced penalties.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor; Class A Misdemeanor (threat to commit a violent felony)
elements: Defendant threatened to commit any offense involving violence
With intent to place the victim in fear of imminent serious bodily injury
enhancements: Threat to commit a violent felony (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Threat of violence against a school is a separate offense with enhanced penalties.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant made a false statement under oath or affirmation
Regarding a material matter
In an official proceeding
The defendant did not believe the statement to be true
notes: Perjury is a Second Degree Felony in Utah — one of the stricter perjury penalties nationwide.

offense_class: Second Degree Felony
elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer any benefit
Upon a public servant
With the purpose of influencing the public servant's action, decision, or vote
notes: Both the person offering and the official accepting may be charged.

offense_class: Third Degree Felony (felony custody); Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor custody)
elements: Defendant was in official custody or confinement
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape
enhancements: Escape from felony custody (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Sentence runs consecutively to any existing sentence.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (subsequent); Third Degree Felony (torture, companion animal)
penalty_max: 6 months (Class B); 364 days (Class A); 5 years (Third Degree)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, recklessly, or with criminal negligence tortured, abused, or cruelly treated an animal
Or failed to provide necessary food, water, care, or shelter
enhancements: Torture of a companion animal (Third Degree Felony)
notes: Aggravated cruelty to animals (torture of a companion animal) is a Third Degree Felony.

offense_class: Determined by original offense classification
penalty_max: Up to the maximum sentence for the original offense
fine_max: Up to the maximum fine for the original offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated one or more conditions of probation
notes: Court may revoke probation and impose the original sentence. Graduated sanctions available for technical violations.

offense_class: Determined by original offense classification
elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated one or more conditions of parole
notes: Board of Pardons and Parole makes revocation decisions.

statute_title: Criminal Responsibility for Conduct of Another
offense_class: Same as the principal offense
elements: A crime was committed by another person
Defendant, acting with the mental state required for the commission of the offense
Solicited, requested, commanded, encouraged, or intentionally aided another to engage in the conduct
notes: Person who aids or encourages is criminally responsible as if they committed the offense.

offense_class: One degree lower than the target offense
penalty_max: Varies by class of the attempted offense
fine_max: Varies by class of the attempted offense
elements: Defendant, acting with the kind of culpability required for the commission of the offense
Engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward commission of the offense
notes: Attempt is generally one degree lower than the completed offense. Attempt to commit a First Degree Felony is a Second Degree Felony.

offense_class: One degree lower than the target offense
penalty_max: Varies by class of the target offense
fine_max: Varies by class of the target offense
elements: Defendant, intending that conduct constituting a crime be performed
Agreed with one or more persons to engage in or cause the performance of such conduct
Any one of them committed an overt act in pursuance of the conspiracy
notes: Conspiracy is one degree lower than the target offense. Requires an overt act. Renunciation is an affirmative defense.
